title: Coherence-first Quant Tuning Playbook
author: Maya Chen
body:
Summary:

This playbook defines the "Coherence-first Quant Tuning" (CFQT) process for promoting quantized model artifacts into Redwood inference environments (hosted, dedicated, private). CFQT prioritizes end-user coherence and semantic consistency over raw token-level loss metrics. It describes probe generation, automated and human-in-the-loop evaluation gates, telemetry thresholds, rollback criteria, and recommended fallback policies for production rollouts.

Scope:

- Applies to all transformer-based text and chat models targeted for 8k and 32k context deployments.
- Intended for quantized artifacts (4-bit, 6-bit, mixed-precision) and hybrid translator artifacts (int8 activations + quantized weights).
- Integrates with the Eval Harness, Model Onboarding pipelines, and the Runtime’s fallback policies.

Definitions and key metrics:

- Coherence Preservation Index (CPI): composite metric combining Structural Coherence (SC), Topicality Agreement (TA), and Response Fluency (RF). Scaled 0..1 where 1 is identical to FP32 baseline. Target: CPI >= 0.94 for promotion.
- Token Preservation Loss (TPL): normalized token log-prob difference aggregated on a workload stratified by prompt-family. Used for near-term triage; TPL <= 0.08 preferred.
- Response Stability Delta (RSD): percent of responses that change semantic class (classification via anchor-based embedding clustering) relative to reference. Threshold: RSD <= 6%.
- 99th percentile latency (p99-RT): measured at synthetic 95th percentile load for target capacity. For hosted SLO: p99-RT <= 320ms for 8k, <= 410ms for 32k on standard GPU profile.

Why coherence-first?

Quantization can reduce model compute and cost, but some quant schemes disproportionately affect coherence (hallucination, instruction-following). CFQT prioritizes user-facing coherence metrics and ties promotion decisions to explicit coherence thresholds rather than only loss/accuracy. This reduces production regressions and customer-facing quality incidents.

Probe generation and workload fingerprinting:

1) Probe families: generate probes by cross-product of: prompt-domain (support, finance, conversational, coding), shot-pattern (0/1/few), context-length (short/mid/long up to the model limit), and adversarial perturbations (typo, truncation, rephrasing, temperature-driven stochastic seeds).
2) Anchor-based seeding: seed probes using live traffic anonymized fingerprints for the tenant or workload class. Use 1-2K probes for tenant shadow runs; 10-20K for global promotion smoke tests.
3) Stratify probes into slices: high-risk (billing/customer-data), instruction-following, multi-turn memory, functioncall signatures. Each slice has distinct CPI and RSD tolerances.

Evaluation gates and automation:

- Gate A (fast): runs token-level checks (TP L, perplexity delta) and throughput/latency smoke tests. Pass if TPL <= 0.12 AND p99-RT within 125% of baseline. Expected run time: < 20 minutes.
- Gate B (coherence): runs CFQT probe suite, computes CPI and RSD per slice, runs automated behavioral tests for hallucination (synthetic knowledge checks). Pass if CPI >= 0.94 AND RSD <= 6% across priority slices. Expected run time: 2-4 hours.
- Gate C (shadow): deploy to shadow fleet with production traffic mirror for 24–72 hours. Collect regression signals (telemetry below). Manual review required if any slice failure occurs.

Promotion decision matrix (automated summary):

- Green: Gates A+B passed, shadow stability within tolerances, automated roll to 10% canary.
- Amber: Gate A passed, Gate B marginal (CPI 0.90–0.94) — require targeted annotation sample (human) for top 500 anchors; proceed only with manual approval and limited canary (<= 2%).
- Red: Gate A failed OR Gate B failed (CPI < 0.90 or RSD > 10%) — do not promote. Open regression ticket.

Telemetry and production monitoring (real-time hooks):

Instrument the following telemetry with per-model and per-tenant shard tagging:

- CPI rolling window (1h/24h) and 7 day trend. Alert if CPI drops by >0.02 in 24h or absolute CPI below 0.92.
- RSD spike detector: alert on >3% increase in 1h.
- Prompt-family drift detector: uses embedding drift and token distribution shift to surface new prompt families causing degraded CPI. Alert threshold: JS divergence > 0.15 vs baseline.
- Safety regressions: hallucination sentinel firing rate (per 1k responses) — escalate if rate doubles vs baseline.

Fallbacks and graceful degradation:

- Per-tenant policy priority: (1) local cached FP32 artifact if present, (2) compatible higher-precision variant in same model family (e.g., 6-bit fallback), (3) remote-hosted FP32 in another region, (4) configured static response or service-unavailable.
- Automatic fallback trigger: CPI < 0.90 sustained over 5 minutes OR RSD spike > 12% OR safety sentinel high confidence.

Runbook: triage steps on a coherence incident (short path for oncall):

1) Identify scope: query telemetry for model-id, tenant, route, time window.
2) If CPI < 0.92 or RSD > 8%: toggle immediate fallback via routing console to previous stable artifact. Notify oncall and model-owner channel.
3) Collect failing probes: generate top 200 differing responses and run delta-analysis tool (eval-harness delta-report).
4) If root cause appears quant-specific (consistent tokens removed, short-circuited attention): label artifact as "quant-degradation" and run quant-tuning matrix (see Appendix YAML).
5) If unclear: escalate to Applied ML oncall and open regression-triage ticket with initial analysis.

Rollout & promotion checklist (must-complete items):

- Model artifact signed and provenance recorded in artifact registry (artifact id, quant config, commit sha).
- CFQT automated report: CPI, TPL, RSD per-slice, and human annotation sample attached.
- Performance baselines attached: p50/p95/p99 latency and tokens/sec at expected concurrency.
- Security & privacy review completed for probe anchors derived from live traffic (DP scrubbed).
- Owner and approver listed with contact details.

Ownership and responsibilities:

- Applied ML team: probe generation, automated CFQT tooling, annotation coordination.
- Serving Runtime team: deployment orchestration, kernel selection, fallback mechanism implementation.
- SRE/Platform: production telemetry, alerting, incident coordination.
- Product & Customer Success: define tenant-specific tolerance and approve amber promotions.

Example CLI and YAML snippets:

- Run CFQT locally via eval-harness helper:

  # run quick coherence gate
  ./eval_harness/run_cfqt.sh --artifact s3://redwood-artifacts/model-x/quant-6bit/ --probe-suite coherence_small --out report.json

- Quant tuning matrix (example):

  quant_tuning:
    artifact_id: "model-x-quant-6b-6bit-20260112"
    steps:
      - name: "activations-int8-sweep"
        params: "int8_activations: [true,false]"
      - name: "scale-aware-gptq"
        params: "clip_range: [0.01, 0.05, 0.1]"
      - name: "kv-cache-precision"
        params: "kv_precision: [fp16, int8_mixed]"

Appendix: example alert policy (pseudocode)

- Alert: CFQT_CPI_Degradation
  condition: CPI(last_1h) - CPI(prev_24h) <= -0.02 OR CPI(last_1h) <= 0.92
  severity: P1
  paging: Applied ML oncall -> Serving Runtime -> SRE
  auto_action: enable_fallback(artifact.previous_stable)

Risk and limitations:

- CPI is an ensemble of heuristics; uncommon prompt families may produce false positives and require human review.
- Shadow runs are necessary for long-tail behavior but expensive for large tenant fleets. Budget these runs into release plans.
